feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: DC shooting leaves 1 person killed, 4 injured. Gunman dead
entry.summary: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.

entry.title: U.S. envoys meet with Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
entry.summary: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff went to the Kremlin to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin and are scheduled to fly later to Ireland for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

entry.title: Indonesia's VP resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
entry.summary: Raka is the son of former President Joko Widodo. The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents that Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.

entry.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal
entry.summary: Huang co-founded the chipmaker Nvidia, which has become one of the driving forces behind the AI boom. But reports that he may have had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy quickly sank his career.

entry.title: A blue wave helped offset for now a falling tally of Black members in the U.S. House
entry.summary: A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now.

entry.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
entry.summary: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

entry.title: Robyn: Tiny Desk Concert
entry.summary: The Swedish star slows her glitchy synth bangers to a more reflective pace, and reaches back to transform the teen pop hit that started it all.

entry.title: Senators don't always share bill text online before votes. They should, advocates say
entry.summary: The text of what lawmakers are considering isn't always made available for public review before it is voted on. A group of open governance advocates is calling on Senate leadership for a change.

entry.title: Kennedy Center plans Ticketmaster switch, raising conflict of interest concerns
entry.summary: The Kennedy Center's former president Richard Grenell was a paid board member of Ticketmaster's parent company at the same time the two parties were negotiating.

entry.title: Trump proposed a 'secret weapon' to police colleges. It will soon become reality
entry.summary: In a 2023 campaign speech, Trump pledged to reclaim universities from what he called the radical left. His Education Department just finalized a rule to help him do it.
